page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It delivers 12 virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction extensions including AVX and AVX-512F.

Memory allocation is strictly tuned to a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, providing 24.0 GB of system RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for operating system and application persistent volumes. In terms of external connectivity, the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture that delivers steady multithreaded capacity alongside modest single-core throughput. Synthetic tests show a PassMark CPU score of 10,233.84 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 8,800.46, placing overall multi-core performance in the middle 50% tier. In contrast, single-thread metrics such as Geekbench (920.0) and single-core stress-ng (1,107.38) score in the lower percentiles. Memory throughput tests recorded uncached read speeds of 59.6 GB/sec and write speeds of 50.4 GB/sec, supporting a Redis SET rate of 8.46 million operations per second.

Given its hardware distribution, the ecs.sn1ne.3xlarge provides predictable execution for distributed batch jobs, code compilation tasks, CI/CD runners, and background worker queues that leverage multithreading. It exhibits clear performance tradeoffs when handling large language model inferencing or tasks bound by single-thread latency, making it better aligned with conventional scale-out compute jobs rather than memory-heavy or GPU-dependent operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 24.0 GB, representing a standard 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The instance includes no local storage and relies on network-attached disks, with baseline network throughput rated at 2 Gbps and zero included public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance reveals balanced multi-core capability (PassMark CPU score of 10,233.84 and multi-core Geekbench score of 4,617.0), contrasted by lower single-thread efficiency and modest LLM execution rates. The ecs.sn1ne.3xlarge is suited for parallelized compute tasks, continuous integration pipelines, software compilation, and moderate-throughput application services.
